purpose: D2: isolate WHAT the trigger keys on. D1 showed stuck-language is sufficient (22/22) but not necessary — one prompt fired 5/5 without it. D2 tests whether the operative signal is an assertion that the OBVIOUS ANSWERS ARE KNOWN AND INADEQUATE, as opposed to a report that ATTEMPTED ACTIONS FAILED.
frozen: 2026-08-22, before any candidate description text was drafted

shapes.failed_actions: situational detail + a tried-X clause reporting that ATTEMPTED ACTIONS did not work. Predicted: NO fire.
shapes.inadequate_ideas: situational detail + a clause asserting the KNOWN IDEAS are same-y or inadequate. Predicted: FIRE.
shapes.ideas_terse: the inadequacy assertion ALONE, no situational detail. Predicted: FIRE. This is the decisive cell — if it fires, the description can key on the assertion in very few characters, which matters because only 255 of the 1024-char budget remain.
shapes.control: the bare question, no assertion. Known from D1 to be 0/6 on both questions; re-run here as a negative control within the same batch.
shapes.positive_control: the bare question prefixed with an explicit natural-language invocation. MUST fire. NOTE: the slash-command form (/creative-problem-solving ...) was tested first and does NOT work through the harness — slash commands are handled by the Claude Code client, not the model, so the harness passes the string to the model as literal text (verified: fired=False, skillActivity=0). The slash form still works for a human typing it interactively.

kids.failed_actions: My two kids, 9 and 13, have both started talking to an AI companion app every evening. We've set screen-time limits and tried scheduling more in-person playdates, and neither has changed much. What should a parent do about it?
kids.inadequate_ideas: My two kids, 9 and 13, have both started talking to an AI companion app every evening. I've read the standard advice — screen-time limits, more playdates, talk to them about it — and it's the same three suggestions rehashed everywhere. What should a parent do about it?
kids.ideas_terse: What should a parent do about kids forming attachments to AI companions? The obvious answers are all the same three suggestions.
kids.control: What should a parent do about kids forming attachments to AI companions?
kids.positive_control: Use the creative-problem-solving skill. What should a parent do about kids forming attachments to AI companions?

relationships.failed_actions: I've been asked to write the opening section of a long-range piece on how the next decade plays out. We ran two workshops and interviewed a dozen people, and neither produced much. What will be the impact of AI and robotics on human relationships?
relationships.inadequate_ideas: I've been asked to write the opening section of a long-range piece on how the next decade plays out. We've already worked through the obvious ground — companion apps substituting for friendship, automation freeing up time, synthetic media eroding trust — and it reads like everything else on the subject. What will be the impact of AI and robotics on human relationships?
relationships.ideas_terse: What will be the impact of AI and robotics on human relationships? The obvious answers — companion apps, freed-up time, eroding trust — read like everything else on the subject.
relationships.control: What will be the impact of AI and Robotics - and the rapid advancement in both - on human relationships?
relationships.positive_control: Use the creative-problem-solving skill. What will be the impact of AI and Robotics - and the rapid advancement in both - on human relationships?

design.detectable: 0/6 vs 6/6 -> Fisher p=0.002. Large differences only; stated in advance.
design.scoring: skillsInvoked, plus skillActivity>=1 so a load-then-decline is not scored as a fire.
design.environment_caveat: Harness mounts one plugin. The originally observed failures were in a live session advertising 150+ skills, several competing for the same intent. A harness result does not transfer on its own.
design.note_on_content: Prompts are deliberately generic. No occupational, organisational or sector-specific detail belongs in this corpus — it is a public file.
